c74object.name: evi_interp
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_interp.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_interp.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
About this File:
Additional interpolation routines not already available in gen~

entry.name: cubic_hermite_interp ( )
entry.description:
Cubic Hermite, McCartney/Harker, 8 muls, 11 ±. Not gen~ [interp mode='cubic']. This is faster than the gen~ cubic (which is the tri-cubic interp from [groove~])
In 1: type=input: f, Interpolator 0..1
In 2: type=input: y0, Current sample minus 2
In 3: type=input: y1, Current sample minus 1
In 4: type=input: y2, Current sample
In 5: type=input: y3, Current sample plus 1
Return 1: Cubic, Cubic interpolated output

entry.name: hermite_sixpoint_interp ( )
entry.description:
Hermite 6-point 5th-order, Olli Niemitalo, 23 muls, 24 ±. Not gen~ [interp mode='spline6']. This is what Niemitalo calls '6-point, 5th-order 2nd-order-osculating z-form implementation' and is actually different to the gen~ 'spline6' which uses the slightly cheaper '6-point, 5th-order B-spline x-form implementation', but which I think is not as useful (the B-spline is not as useful for audio samples representation).
In 1: type=input: f0, Interpolator 0..1
In 2: type=input: ym2, Current sample minus 2
In 3: type=input: ym1, Current sample minus 1
In 4: type=input: y0, Current sample
In 5: type=input: y1, Current sample plus 1
In 6: type=input: y2, Current sample plus 2
In 7: type=input: y3, Current sample plus 3
Return 1: Hermite, Hermite interpolated output
